title: Annual Reward Attribution Between Northgate Memberships
content:
**Article — memberships are never pooled.** When a customer holds both a consumer and a business membership of Northgate Memberships, or is a cardholder on several, the memberships are never pooled. Each purchase earns Annual Reward only on the membership recorded on that purchase — for merchandise, the membership recorded on the purchase in its Northgate Purchases & Returns record; for eyewear, the membership recorded on the Northgate Optical job — and each membership's cap, balance and certificate are computed separately.

**Presented card.** Annual Reward for a purchase accrues only to the membership whose card was presented for it. The membership that earns is the one the company's purchase record shows; the customer's statement of which membership they meant to use does not move it.

**Cardholder purchases.** Purchases made with a household or business add-on card belong to the membership the card is issued on, and earn to it when that tier credits the purchases of household and add-on cardholders to the membership.

**Reversals.** A reversal is always booked on the same membership as the accrual it takes back, found through the source sale line or optical charge, even when the member now presents a different card for the return.

**Transfers and merging.** A member asking to move reward between memberships, or to merge two memberships' balances, is asking for something no Northgate policy provides.

## Attribution at a glance

| Event | Membership that is credited or debited |
|---|---|
| Purchase with the primary member's card | the membership recorded on the purchase |
| Purchase with a household or add-on card | the membership the card is issued on, when that tier credits cardholders' purchases |
| Return, price adjustment, rebate or refund of a rewarded purchase | the membership that earned the original accrual, whatever card is presented for the return |
| Request to move reward, or merge balances, between memberships | not provided by any Northgate policy |

## Hypothetical cases

- A member holds a Northgate Club Plus Membership and a Northgate Business Plus Membership and buys merchandise presenting the business card. The purchase record shows the business membership; only the business membership earns on it, against the business membership's own cap.
- The same member later returns that merchandise presenting the consumer card. The reversal is booked on the business membership, the one whose accrual it takes back.
- The member asks for the reward earned on the business membership to be added to the consumer membership's balance. No Northgate policy provides for it.
